Charpy strength
1 value

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
7 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
10 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Good for
“Fiberon™ PETG-ESD offers electrostatic discharge (ESD) safety with improved toughness making it a good candidate for applications in electronics industry.” data sheet, p. 1
“Electronics housings and enclosures” the maker's product page (marketing text), p. 1: Description, Ideal Applications

“Jigs and fixtures for PCB assembly” the maker's product page (marketing text), p. 1: Description, Ideal Applications
Scope and conditions: Maker intended use only. Load, lifetime, printed geometry and qualification absent; no selection pass or suitability rule. ESD function needs finished-part validation under use conditions.
“Trays and storage for electronic components” the maker's product page (marketing text), p. 1: Description, Ideal Applications
Scope and conditions: Maker intended use only. Load, lifetime, printed geometry and qualification absent; no selection pass or suitability rule. ESD function needs finished-part validation under use conditions.
“Tools and parts used in ESD-sensitive environments” the maker's product page (marketing text), p. 1: Description, Ideal Applications
Scope and conditions: Maker intended use only. Load, lifetime, printed geometry and qualification absent; no selection pass or suitability rule. ESD function needs finished-part validation under use conditions.
Pitfalls and limitations
“Nozzle temperature and print orientation strongly affect surface resistivity. Higher nozzle temperatures lower resistivity; validate the finished part for the intended ESD requirement.” the maker's product page (marketing text), p. 1: Printing Tips, ESD validation
Scope and conditions: Own product-specific sensitivity statement, not a universal ESD pass. Own TDS surface-resistivity table remains temperature/orientation-specific.
“Advanced Carbon Nanotube Compounding This filament is compounded with carbon nanotubes, which are responsible for its ESD-safe properties. The use of carbon nanotubes ensures consistent conductivity throughout the printed part, maintaining ESD protection even after machining or wear.” the maker's product page (marketing text), p. 1: Description, composition and wear claim
Scope and conditions: Maker compounding/ESD-after-wear claim without test conditions; own FAQ says ESD can degrade with surface abrasion/humidity/temperature/contaminants. Contradiction retained; no permanent durability result.
“The ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) safety of PETG-ESD filament can degrade over time, depending on environmental factors like humidity, temperature, and exposure to dust or contaminants. PETG-ESD filaments contain conductive additives, which can wear off or lose effectiveness due to surface abrasion or environmental wear. Typically, the ESD-safe properties should remain intact for 1-2 years under controlled conditions, but regular testing is recommended to ensure continued ESD performance. Storing parts in a clean, dry environment can help maintain their ESD properties longer.” the maker's product page (marketing text), p. 1: FAQ, ESD lifetime
Scope and conditions: Own FAQ lifecycle narrative with undefined controlled conditions. The1–2year figure is not an accepted measured lifetime or warranty, and conflicts with the unqualified wear claim. Finished parts require testing.

Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00063

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis... polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

Hot water or moist air at higher temperatures · limited
Polycondensation products, to which polyamides also belong, have a limited resistance to hot water or moist air at higher temperatures. PA 12 has good hydrolysis resistance compared to other polyamides, but it is gradually molecularly degraded by hot water. Compounds with a high molecular mass will last longer than those with a low molecular mass. Hydrolytic degradation occurs faster in acid media than in neutral or alkaline media. Standard compounds are resistant to pure water to about 70 or 80 °C.

Exposure to short wave light of wavelengths less than 400 nm results in an accelerated decrease in the molecular mass of the polymers, causing molded parts and semi-finished products to become brittle. Light stabilizers, UV absorbers and/or radical scavengers considerably reduce weathering damage. Izod impact strength
10 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
2 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

Charpy strength
2 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
3 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Hydrolytic stability: limited polymer-level M160-hydrolysis
Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU) · not resistant · can screen
If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. This results in a reduction in mechanical properties. This effect is more marked in flexible grades. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
5 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

tabs.Coverage:
Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00064

Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00063

Charpy strength
22 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Hydrolytic stability: limited polymer-level M053-hydrolysis
Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis... polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.
High temperature
Polymer-level reference for PA12, not this product · source: EMS-GRIVORY, Technical Data Sheet Grilon, Grilamid and Grivory – Resistance to Chemicals, p. 3 Hydrolysis resistance PB00209
Hot water or moist air at higher temperatures · limited
Polycondensation products, to which polyamides also belong, have a limited resistance to hot water or moist air at higher temperatures. PA 12 has good hydrolysis resistance compared to other polyamides, but it is gradually molecularly degraded by hot water. Compounds with a high molecular mass will last longer than those with a low molecular mass. Hydrolytic degradation occurs faster in acid media than in neutral or alkaline media. Standard compounds are resistant to pure water to about 70 or 80 °C.

Exposure to short wave light of wavelengths less than 400 nm results in an accelerated decrease in the molecular mass of the polymers, causing molded parts and semi-finished products to become brittle. Light stabilizers, UV absorbers and/or radical scavengers considerably reduce weathering damage. However, the best protection is provided by suitable grades of carbon black, if blackening is possible.

All of them stay on record and are shown here.

58 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
25 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. 58 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
10 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. Charpy strength
1 value

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

No record of this material's own; what follows is its base polymer's published behaviour.

FROM THE BASE POLYMER ABS
In these 5 categories no source tested this material or its products, so the published behaviour of the neat ABS resin is shown instead, from a resin producer's or handbook reference. It is not a test of this grade: fillers, pigments and printing change it. It never passes a requirement; where the reference reports the polymer attacked or dissolved (organic solvent resistance), it screens this material out of that requirement with "Let estimates rule out materials" on, and the SCREENED chip brings it back.

Charpy strength
6 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
3 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

FROM THE BASE POLYMER ASA
In these 5 categories no source tested this material or its products, so the published behaviour of the neat ASA resin is shown instead, from a resin producer's or handbook reference. It is not a test of this grade: fillers, pigments and printing change it. It never passes a requirement; where the reference reports the polymer attacked or dissolved (organic solvent resistance), it screens this material out of that requirement with "Let estimates rule out materials" on, and the SCREENED chip brings it back.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00063

A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00062

Charpy strength
1 value

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
7 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
3 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

All of them stay on record and are shown here.

A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
25 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
58 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
1 value

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
10 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.
